subject: Private deployment - network evidence & diagram-lite deliverable
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orchidhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@orchidhealth.com>, Orchid Health Procurement <procure@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Private deploy network evidence + abbreviated diagram

Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Orchid's security team has a narrow ask: a concise evidence pack that covers the network isolation model for the private deployment we discussed, plus a lightweight diagram and a small inventory matrix we can attach to our SIG/CAIQ submission. Specifically they want: 1) a one-page diagram that shows tenant vs control-plane boundaries, egress choke points, and KMS/HSM boundaries; 2) an inventory table (component, VPC/subnet, security group, data classification); 3) a short narrative (300–500 words) tying the diagram to SOC 2 controls (network segmentation, egress filtering, audit logging).

Our timeline: can we get a draft by EOD 2026-12-10? We know you have a heavier architecture packet — this is intentionally "diagram-lite" for procurement and our compliance reviewers. If possible, please include any CAIQ mapping rows that are already done for network-related attributes.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Senior InfoSec Program Manager
Orchid Health

Attachments requested: CAIQ template (network sections), example SOC 2 control ids
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>

Date: 2026-12-07T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private deploy network evidence + abbreviated diagram

Kimberly/Ben —

Looping you in for the diagram-lite deliverable Emily from Orchid asked for. Goal: compact, customer-facing artifact that stands alone for procurement reviewers. Priority items:
- One-page diagram (PDF) with tenant overlay, control-plane demarcation, egress point(s), and KMS/HSM callouts.
- Inventory matrix (CSV) with component, role (control vs tenant), VPC/subnet, security controls applied (NACL/SG), and data classification.
- 400-word narrative tying back to SOC 2 Network Security & System Operations controls; include a short note on audit log retention and how we surface flow logs.

Kimberly: can you take the diagram and narrative? Use the simplified topology from the private deploy runbook (no raw infra screenshots). Ben: can you assemble the inventory matrix and pull the CIDR/SG names. Marissa: once assembled, please sanity-check the CAIQ mapping rows (if any) and the Drive link we'll hand over. Emily asked for a draft by EOD 12/10.

I'll send a short checklist to attach with the artifacts.

-Jordan
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T14:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private deploy network evidence + abbreviated diagram

Jordan/Ben/Marissa —

Progress update and attached stubs: network-diagram-lite.pdf (single-sheet), inventory-matrix.csv, segmentation-narrative.docx. High-level notes that will go into the 400-word narrative:

- Control plane separation: Control-plane services (orchestration, model registry, telemetry) run in a dedicated management VPC. Tenant inference workloads are pinned to customer-specific tenant VPCs that are logically isolated by VPC peering and strict routing policies. Control plane endpoints are accessible only through an authenticated API gateway and private interconnects; no control-plane public-facing admin endpoints are allowed.

- Egress control: Tenant VPCs egress strictly through a managed NAT + centralized egress proxy located in an outbound egress VPC. Egress flows are filtered using network ACLs and a set of approved destination lists maintained by Network Security. Flow logs (VPC Flow Logs + proxy access logs) are retained for 180 days in a customer-tagged bucket (subject to contract).

- KMS/HSM boundary: Customer data encryption keys are stored in customer-managed KMS where requested; for Redwood-managed keys we use HSM-backed KMS with dedicated key rings per customer where required by contract. Key usage is audited and key access is role-restricted; include reference to our KMS audit export process in the narrative.

- Audit & detection: Flow logs + agent telemetry are aggregated to our observability pipeline with per-tenant indices. We call out SOC 2 control mappings for network security (NW-1, NW-2 equivalents) and note that alerting thresholds are documented in the runbook.

Deliverables attached as stubs for review. Items outstanding: final CIDR names for three tenant VPC examples (Ben to confirm), a CAIQ row export for network items (Marissa).

-Kim
Senior Security Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments included: network-diagram-lite.pdf (diagram stub), inventory-matrix.csv (partial), segmentation-narrative.docx (draft)
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@orchidhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@orchidhealth.com>, Orchid Health Procurement <procure@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T15:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private deploy network evidence + abbreviated diagram

Jordan/Kim —

Thanks — this looks great as a starting point. We pulled the PDF and inventory CSV from the Drive link you shared and the narrative reads well for reviewers. A couple of quick clarifications before procurement can move forward: 1) Can you add an explicit line to the narrative that states retention windows for VPC Flow Logs and proxy logs (you referenced 180 days but Procurement wants the explicit policy id or contract clause reference if available)? 2) For the KMS boundary, can you confirm whether customer-managed keys are supported in the private deployment in our EU region as well (we have an EU-hosted workload)? 3) Finally, could you export the CAIQ rows that map to network-related attributes and put them in a single CSV for our SIG pack?

If you can get those three items in a follow-up by EOD 2026-12-13 we should be able to attach to the procurement packet.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emily
Senior InfoSec Program Manager, Orchid Health
